main_body: two-story timber and stone building with hipped tile roof
top_band: tiled roof slope from row 0 to row 42 (orange/red-brown tiles with yellow ridge highlight at rows 2-3)
evidence: The building shows a large foreshortened tiled roof top surface (rows 0-42, plus chimney opening at rows 0-4) overhanging the two-story south wall (rows 43-107). A dark eave shadow band sits at rows 43-50 under the roof edge, and the windows and door are recessed into the wall.

style.evidence: The candidate is an authentic Beodeul building sharing the exact same tile roof, chimney, plaster speckle, timber framing, and cobblestone wall tiles as the two reference houses.
